course_title: Design Computing Studio I - Interactive Technology
course_description:
This course introduces students to studio-based learning and the Design Computing studio stream. Students work in small teams to design, iterate and implement user-centred design computing projects. Consolidating skills and knowledge from prior studies, students will move through concept and proposal to develop their designs using interactive technologies, keeping in mind the human and ethical impacts of their work. Through their individual work and the team project, students will begin to develop important skills such as problem solving, project management, team collaboration and design communication.

This course introduces students to the design process as it relates to the domain of interaction design and information technology. Students will be able to apply their understanding of technology, coding, and design, gained in previous courses such as DECO1400 and CSSE1001 to an iterative design project. Working in small teams, students will follow an iterative, user-centred design process to design and prototype interactive solutions in response to a given brief. Students will be introduced to methods and skills for the generation, refinement, and implementation of their solutions, including critical reflection, project scoping, and ethical impact analysis. Students will develop the ability to communicate design ideas effectively, identify different design approaches, and assess the impact and outcomes of these approaches on both their users and society as a whole. Additionally, they will gain skills in managing team-based projects, including conflict resolution and effective collaboration skills. These skills will be applicable in future studio subjects, including Design Computing Studio 2 and 3. At the end of the semester, students will present their work to teaching staff and peers at a final tradeshow.

This year, in response to student feedback, the assessment has be refined to incorporate the Studio Design Journal into the Portfolio. Portfolio checkpoints have been introduced to provide students feedback on their progress as the semester unfolds.

AI tools may be used in this course, and students receive guidance on acceptable use, attribution or disclosure. Students are responsible for ensuring that any use of AI complies with academic integrity requirements and is appropriately acknowledged. Students will be required to submit a Statement of Work with each assessment item that explicitly identifies both original and non-original work in the submission; and clearly describes any use of AI or MT used to inform the design or the production of the work.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse and propose design computing solutions that aligns with the objectives and constraints of a project brief.
Understand key course concepts and studio workflow and apply those principles in an iterative development process.
Apply design and technical skills within a multidisciplinary team to build a proof-of-concept prototype.
Apply critical thinking to reflect on and analyse the development and outcome of a project, considering how well they align with user needs and the project brief.
Recognise ethical implications of design decisions and describe their potential impact on users, communities, and stakeholders.
Apply teamwork and communication strategies to collaborate effectively, resolve conflict, and contribute to shared project goals.
Present design decisions, design process and outcomes clearly through visual, oral and written communication.

assessment_details.title: Design Activities
assessment_details.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Participation/ Student contribution, Reflection, Tutorial/ Problem Set
assessment_details.task_description: Each week, you will be assigned design activities linked to weekly studio and practical sessions that support the development of design knowledge, technical skills and project work. Activities may include design exercises, critiques, readings, reflections, technical challenges, or responses to weekly course content. The activities provide the opportunity to apply concepts introduced in class, document learning as it occurs, and receive feedback on developing ideas and skills. Together, the design activities provide evidence of your individual engagement, progress and contributions throughout the semester. They also support the development of your team project and Design Portfolio. Use of AI and Machine Translation tools This assessment is designed to help students develop and apply user-centred design methods, design thinking, and reflective practice in authentic studio contexts. Success in this assessment requires active participation in design activities, critical engagement with users, teams, and project challenges, and the ability to apply course concepts to specific design situations. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use Generative AI technologies, successful completion of this task will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. Generative AI Tools and techniques may be utilized as supportive elements. However, there are boundaries to your usage of Generative AI Tools. Going beyond those boundaries amounts to an academic integrity issue. Where applicable, students will be required to attach a Statement of Work to their design activity outcome that explicitly identifies both original and non-original work in the submission; and clearly describes any use of AI or MT used to inform the design or the production of the work. Because this assessment evaluates your developing reflective and design practice, you must clearly acknowledge any external tools, including Generative AI, used in preparing portfolio content. The feedback provided is formative and intended to help you strengthen the quality of your evidence, reflections, and portfolio structure before the final submission. assessment_details.task_description: The Design Portfolio documents your individual learning, contributions, and development throughout the semester. Drawing on evidence collected during studio activities and project work, the portfolio should showcase key examples of your design practice, including your process, decision-making, skills development, and contribution to the team project. More than a collection of artefacts, the portfolio is an annotated reflection on your design journey. You should curate and present selected evidence of your work, explaining what you did, why you did it, what you learned, and how your thinking evolved through collaboration, feedback, and iteration. The portfolio is both a record of your work and a design artefact in its own right. It should be organised, visually effective, and communicate your individual contribution within the broader context of the team project. Strong portfolios demonstrate not only what was produced, but also how challenges were addressed, decisions were made, and learning occurred throughout the semester. The portfolio will be developed through the following milestones: Portfolio Draft & Plan due in Week 7 , at this checkpoint, your will submit a draft of your portfolio, including a progress review, reflection on learning to date and a plan for the remainder of the semester. See assessment item Portfolio Draft & Plan for more information. Design Portfolio due in Exam Week 1 , you will submit your final portfolio demonstrating contributions, learning, professional growth and critical reflection across the semester. You are encouraged to draw on evidence generated through the Design Activities assessment, project activities, workshop exercises, feedback, and project artefacts to support your reflections and demonstrate learning throughout the semester. See assessment item Design Portfolio for more information. assessment_details.task_description: Following the submission of your final portfolio, you will undertake a Portfolio Review Interview. During this interview, you will have 3-5 minutes to present the highlights from your portfolio as a precursor to a 5 -7 minute Q&A session with teaching staff. Questions will focus on understanding the contributions you made to the team project and your learning in the course. You should focus reflections on the work you have completed through course activities, through self-directed learning and through the project - reflecting on your role in the success (or failure) of the team project. You will use the content of your portfolio to evidence the work you have done. Use of MT/AI Tools for the Portfolio presentation & interview This assessment task is to be completed in-person.
